demographics.trauma_type: Accidentally caused serious injury to another

vignette: John, a 54-year-old North American forester, spends his days navigating through dense forests and coordinating logging operations. His job requires him to be meticulous and detail-oriented, yet he finds it increasingly difficult to concentrate on the task at hand since the accident four months ago. John had been working with a team to clear a path for new growth when an unexpected shift in the terrain caused a heavy branch to fall. Despite his best efforts to warn his colleagues, one of them was struck and seriously injured. Since that day, John has become a different man. Once confident and capable, he now wrestles with intense guilt and anxiety. He often wakes up drenched in sweat from nightmares where he relives the moment the branch fell and imagines the shock and pain on his colleague's face. The images are vivid and intrusive, making it nearly impossible for him to sleep without tossing and turning. John's wife, Sarah, has noticed a significant change in his behavior. He is withdrawn and irritable, often snapping at her over minor things. She finds him pacing around the house late into the night, muttering apologies under his breath. He avoids social gatherings and even skips church on Sundays, unable to bear being surrounded by people who might remind him of the incident. At work, John's performance has also taken a hit. His concentration is shot; he can't seem to focus for more than a few minutes at a time without getting lost in thoughts about what happened. He keeps replaying the accident over and over in his mind, wondering if there was something he could have done differently. The weight of responsibility presses on him heavily, making it hard to trust his own judgment. His coworkers have begun to notice John's struggle as well. He often isolates himself during lunch breaks and has developed a habit of checking equipment repeatedly, convinced that another accident is just waiting to happen. His meticulous nature, once an asset in the field, has turned into a form of self-punishment. Every tool, every piece of machinery-John sees potential danger lurking everywhere. During his rare moments of clarity, John feels overwhelming guilt. He questions why he survived when others did not and wonders if his colleague will ever forgive him. The fear that he might cause another accident haunts him constantly. On particularly bad days, he considers quitting his job altogether but knows deep down that it's the only thing grounding him. John's wife tries to be supportive, encouraging him to open up about what he's going through. Yet, even when Sarah is there for him, John often pushes her away, feeling as though he doesn't deserve her love and support. The emotional distance between them has grown palpable, leaving both of them struggling with the strain. Despite his best efforts to push these thoughts aside, John can't escape the recurring memories that flood his mind at random moments-like when he hears a branch snap or sees a fallen log on the side of the road. Each time, he feels a sharp pang of guilt and fear, as if he's reliving the trauma all over again. John's life has become an endless loop of flashbacks, hypervigilance, and avoidance. The once-simple act of walking through a forest now triggers intense anxiety, making him question every step. His days are filled with worry about another accident happening and whether he'll be able to prevent it if it does. His relationship with Sarah is strained as she watches her husband suffer silently, unsure how to help or even approach the subject without causing more pain. John's work has become a place of both comfort and torment-a sanctuary where he feels somewhat in control but also a reminder of his ongoing struggle. John's days are an exhausting mix of trying to maintain his composure while battling intense waves of guilt and anxiety. He knows he can't keep living this way, yet the road ahead seems daunting and uncertain. For now, he continues to navigate through his daily life with a heavy heart, hoping for some semblance of peace amidst the chaos.
